title: Mother will 'never forgive' her toddler's killer, court hears
text: Mother will 'never forgive' her toddler's killer, court hears A woman whose former partner murdered her two-year-old child on the NSW Mid North Coast has spoken in court about her devastating loss. The man was sentenced in the Supreme Court of NSW after being found guilty of the murder charges in July. A woman whose former partner murdered her two-year-old child has told the NSW Supreme Court she will never forgive him. The sentencing hearing will resume on December 2. A woman whose former partner murdered her two-year-old child on the NSW Mid North Coast has told a court she will never forgive his killer. Members of the child's family gave victim impact statements during a sentencing hearing in the NSW Supreme Court in Sydney today. A 40-year-man, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was found guilty of the boy's murder by a jury after a four-week trial earlier this year.At the time of the baby's death in 2022, the man was in a relationship and living with the child's mother.\"He changed my life in ways that can never be undone. I'll never forgive him,\" she said. The man was charged after a coronial inquest into the child's death in September 2024 found there was enough evidence to suggest he may have been involved.During the trial, the jury heard that on the morning of May 23, 2022, the toddler's mother found the child unresponsive when she tried to wake him.to Newcastle's John Hunter Hospital, where he died of a catastrophic brain injury two days later. The two-year-old died in hospital in May 2022. The jury heard evidence that the offender would discipline the child by locking him in a dark garage with the lights off or by taking away his mattress and pillow.On the afternoon before his death, the court heard the toddler's mother saw him fall downstairs outside their home.the child's father told the court about the devastating impact of\"My enjoyment of life has been sucked out of my soul.\" A statement was read in court on behalf of the boy’s older brother, who said he was angry \"he isn't here anymore\". \"I have all of his toys in my room but it's not really fun to play with them myself. \"\"These are questions I ask myself daily and will spend the rest of my years trying to make sense ,\" she said.Defence barrister David Price told the court that he planned to subpoena medicalthe offender's diagnosis of multiple sclerosis included in sentencing considerations.\"Leaving it until after proceedings and after being convicted of murder is unsatisfactory,\" he said. The sentencing hearing will continue on December 2.
summary: A woman whose former partner murdered her two-year-old child on the NSW Mid North Coast has told a court she will never forgive his killer. Members of the child's family gave victim impact statements during a sentencing hearing in the NSW Supreme Court in Sydney today.
